headline: China and Russia both speak out Monday against renewed military action on Iran as Doha draft circulates with no breakthrough

However, the…
sources: Reuters wire, 'Iran says contacts over ending war continue as talks end with no breakthrough'
fault_line: Diplomacy or post-midterm strike? Beijing and Moscow publicly push talks while Tehran's own sources say they expect bombs, not a deal, once the US vote is over.

sections.what_happened: Contacts between Iran and the US to end their eight-month war are continuing through mediators after days of Iranian talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday ('the dialogues are continuing. However, the issue is complex'). As fears grow the conflict could reignite after Tuesday's US midterm elections, China and Russia both spoke out Monday against renewed military action: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said after meeting senior Iranian security official Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing that all parties should focus on political solutions rather than resorting to arms again (Chinese statement, also carried by AFP via Dawn's live blog), and Russia's Foreign Ministry said reports of new military action against Iran were a cause for 'extreme concern' and called for increased diplomatic efforts. Iranian sources told Reuters they believed a new US attack was still more likely than a deal. Trump has repeatedly said there would be no new attack before Tuesday's vote.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) for the full item; AFP (T1) via Dawn live blog for the Wang Yi/Beijing-support element; Chinese and Russian foreign-ministry statements are the primary sources as reported
sections.what_disputed: No US response to the Chinese/Russian statements in-window; the 'attack more likely than deal' judgement comes from unnamed Iranian sources, not an official statement; Baghaei's 'contacts continuing' does not equal a deal -- the Doha draft remains unaccepted by Washington (standing position, 1800-01).
sections.why_matters: While the Doha draft circulates with no breakthrough, China and Russia just lined up against a post-midterm strike -- and Tehran's own sources say they expect the strike anyway.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Reuters published 09:36Z, updated 13:27Z = 17:27 ; missed by the 1800 scan) -- China and Russia both speak out Monday against renewed military action on Iran as Doha draft circulates with no breakthrough

totw_analysis: Our read: While the Doha draft circulates with no breakthrough, China and Russia just lined up against a post-midterm strike -- and Tehran's own sources say they expect the strike anyway. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Diplomacy or post-midterm strike? Beijing and Moscow publicly push talks while Tehran's own sources say they expect bombs, not a deal, once the US vote is over.
